Show HN: ChillSweep – A better cleaner app for PC and Mac
items.summary: I was frustrated with the manual busy work of cleaning appdata leftovers and how much most traditional cleaner apps miss. Most cleaners I've used in the past simply check a fixed list of common junk folders. I've been playing around with an app idea I've called ChillSweep, a free, open-source cleanup tool for Windows and Mac. ChillSweep checks folders against what's actually installed on your machine, and can claim back huge amounts of disk space other cleaners can't see. Download: github.com/terranivium/chillsweep/releases/latest

Show HN: A virtual recording studio where you direct session players
items.summary: Hi HN. I'm Hunter, one of the co-founders of Daydream, a small music research lab. Our research focus is musical control. Musicians steer each other by a shared set of rules: the chart, the groove, who's carrying the melody. We are building control models with real-time performance and an actual understanding of music. Our core real-time engine is open source and can be found here: https://github.com/daydreamlive/DEMON The preview I'm sharing is an in-browser recording studio with virtual session players you can direct in real time. You record, upload, or generate a source track. Then you book "session players" and build your way to a full song.

items.title: Show HN: The Last SaaS – An open source headless SaaS for agents and assistants
items.summary: This kind of started as a joke, and it still kind of is. But it's also kind of fun to think about what the minimum number of primitives would cover all possible typical SaaS applications. And then drive that from an agent/assistant. There is obvious stuff like CRUD, and then permissions, users, notifications etc. So basically I made a start of a "headless SaaS" that has no UI and is just a CLI/API/MCP that you can connect your Claude etc to and it can make the UIs and displays in real time when you need it. This isn't like a startup. I'm more curious about your opinions about how much of SaaS can just be replaced. It can be backed by SQLite(or Postgres), so it's super quick to self-host, but you can also use the hosted version for free to test it out. The repo is at https://github.com/mkly/thelastsaas The website that demonstrates basic usage and installation: https://thelastsaas.com The main app is at https://app.thelastsaas.com There is both a CLI and an MCP available. Both have the same functionality. Thanks for taking a look. Suggestions and feedback greatly appreciated.

items.title: Show HN: Checkout this open-source, local-first bioinformatics/AI desktop app
items.summary: So the basic idea behind Liatir is to have a desktop environment that works like a virtual lab for bioinformatics to do your work locally, without having to send data to a cloud service or glue together a bunch of separate tools and interfaces. You shouldn’t need to write a single line of code to use it, but if you do know how to code, it's as extensible as you want it to be with the plugin system supporting Node, Python and Rust. It provides regular bioinformatics tools, local scientific AI models, integrations with workflow systems such as Nextflow, API calls when you need to connect to external data or environments, scientific viewers, and visual pipelines that tie all of those pieces together. Oh and the AI models are self-contained boxes so you do not need to set up anything and just run them. Hope you'll find this interesting.
